title: Prefill occupancy oddities — debugging journal
content:
Quick summary:
Observed a sustained throughput drop (~20-35% QPS) on model-runner-4 during the 11/01 - 11/08 window while p99 latency stayed within expected bounds for most requests. Initial hypothesis was CPU/GPU contention; secondary hypothesis is continuous-batching + prefill misconfiguration leaving lots of 'occupied' but underfilled slots (low occupancy) and causing inefficient kernel launches.

Environment & scope:
- Cluster: prod-eu-west-2 (subset of Dedicated pool: rdw-ded-4)
- Affected nodes: model-runner-4 (gpu-a100-80GB), model-runner-7 (same pool, intermittent)
- Model: open-llm-3b (optimized-qat variant)
- Workload: short-chat queries, median seq_len ~ 40, 95pct ~ 120; lots of short-prefill followed by short generation

Observed metrics (prom snippets):
- Node GPU utilization: 65-75% (was 80-95% baseline)
- GPU SMs active vs kernel time: kernel time per-token increased ~12%
- Average batch size measured at runtime: 3.2 (expected 5.0 for these traffic patterns)
- Prefill occupancy ratio metric (prefill_occupied_tokens / prefill_capacity): 0.28 (target ~0.6)
- Queue depth (requests waiting to be batched): low (often 0-2) — indicates not lack of work but batching failing to coalesce

Concrete traces/logs (redacted IDs):
- Admin trace for one impacted request: trace_id=tr-11-0802-9f3
  - router: accepted request t=0ms
  - batcher: scheduled to window id=win-203 (max-wait-ms=10)
  - prefill: started fill for req_id=req-790, prefill_slots=4, claimed=4, filled=1 (most slots remained zero-filled)
  - runtime: issued kernel launch for batch size=4; internal note: kv_prefill_miss_count=3
  - result: generation time higher than expected, downstream retry 0

- Pod logs (kubectl logs model-runner-4 -n rdw):
  [2025-11-07T03:12:10Z] batcher: window_open id=win-203 max_wait_ms=10 max_batch_tokens=4096 occupancy_threshold=0.5
  [2025-11-07T03:12:10Z] prefill: prefill_alloc slots=4 slot_size=256 token_map: [req-790:40, gap, gap, gap]
  [2025-11-07T03:12:10Z] prefill: kv_lookup hit=1 miss=3
  [2025-11-07T03:12:10Z] runtime: launch kernels for batch_size=4 seqs=[40,1,1,1] -> padding_injected=3
  [2025-11-07T03:12:10Z] perf: per_token_latency=0.012s baseline=0.010s

Commands I ran (sanitized):
- Query router debug (returns trace headers):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "x-rw-debug: trace" https://api.redwood.int/v1/route/trace/req-790 | jq .

- Prom queries used to build the above snippets:
  - avg by (node) (rate(runtime_tokens_total[5m]))
  - ratio(prefill_occupied_tokens_total, prefill_capacity_total)
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))

- Pod-level checks:
  kubectl -n rdw exec -it model-runner-4 -- /bin/sh -c "cat /var/log/rw/runtime/batcher.log | tail -n 200"
  kubectl -n rdw top pod model-runner-4

- Temporary repro (staging): replayed short-chat load with seq len distribution skewed to 10-50 tokens using load-generator tool; toggled batcher config live via /admin/batcher/config endpoint to observe occupancy changes.

Hypotheses (in rough priority order):
1) Prefill allocation policy is over-allocating slot counts per window (claiming 4 slots but many are for tiny sequences), causing kernel padding overhead. That + low occupancy leads to lower GPU efficiency.
2) A recent change in continuous-batcher heuristics (PR #4321) introduced an aggressive "min-claim" fallback when queue_depth < 3 that causes windows to pre-claim but not wait for arrivals. Works fine for larger-seq workloads but bad for short-chat workloads.
3) KV-prefill cache TTL misalignment: TTL too short, so lookups are frequently misses, leading to prefill holes. Misses then get padded, amplifying inefficiency for short sequences.
4) Timing skew: clock drift between router and batcher means many requests hit the early max-wait cutoff and windows close prematurely. Less likely given cluster time-sync metric OK.

Experiments run so far (results):
- Reproduce in staging: replay with same intensity -> saw avg batch size drop from 5.1 -> 3.4 when continuous-batcher enabled with new PR config (reproducible).
- Toggle min-claim to 1 (from 3): avg batch size increased to 4.6, throughput recovered ~18% in staging within 10 minutes. Memory/latency tradeoff OK.
- Increase kv_prefill_ttl to 600s in staging: hit rate improved (kv_prefill_hit_rate +6%), occupancy ratio +0.08, but alone did not fully recover baseline.
- Increase max-wait-ms from 10 -> 30 on a canary: batch size increased but p99 latency also increased marginally (~+60ms). Tradeoff could be acceptable if SLOs allow.

Immediate mitigation applied to prod canary (model-runner-4):
- rolled back min-claim fallback to previous setting (min-claim=1). Rollout via feature flag (ff-batcher-min-claim) to 10% nodes at 03:30 UTC 2025-11-08.
- turned up kv_prefill_ttl to 300s on canary nodes.
Outcome: throughput on canary nodes improved ~15% within 20 minutes, p99 stable. Still under baseline but trending up.

Risks/notes:
- Increasing max-wait-ms helps occupancy but increases tail latency; must weigh against SLOs and customer-facing expectations.
- Longer kv_prefill_ttl increases memory for cache store (Redis/rocksdb footprint) and could affect eviction patterns. Monitor cache size and evictions.
- Reverting PR #4321 may reintroduce other regressions for long-seq workloads; need a more targeted rollout (traffic routing by seq_len).

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run a small A/B: route short-chat traffic to nodes with older batcher heuristics, long-chat to new heuristics (canary run). Measure token efficiency and p99 separately.
- [ ] Add a metric: batch_window_fill_ratio (fraction of claimed slots that have >1 token) exported per-window to make this visible in dashboards.
- [ ] Add a permanent canary config: for seq_len_median < 60 use min-claim=1 and max-wait-ms=25 automatically.
- [ ] Follow up with infra to evaluate memory delta if kv_prefill_ttl is globally increased to 600s.
- [ ] Postmortem stub: /confluence/infra/prefill-occupancy-postmortem (link placeholder)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Watch out for optimism bias: quick rollbacks can mask root cause. We should capture a 24h window of traces from both before/after change.
- If we end up patching heuristics, add unit tests simulating heavy short-chat traffic (seq_len histogram) so PRs can't regress this again.

Scratch commands I might still run:
- Dump a few raw batch traces for deeper analysis:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.int/admin/debug/batch-trace?window_id=win-203 | jq . > /tmp/win-203.json

- Compare kernels launched stats across nodes:
  ssh runner-4 "cat /sys/fs/rw/perf/kernel_launch_stats.log" | sed -n '1,120p'

- Quick grep for PRs touching batcher heuristics in last 30 days:
  git log --since='30 days' --oneline -- rw-runtime/batcher | grep -i claim

If anyone else is poking at this, leave a note in slack #eng-runtime with trace id and canary tag; I put up a small dashboard under devdash/prefill-occupancy.

End of journal entry for now.
